gen_risks.description: Inadequate benefit levels of social protection programs may hinder their effectiveness in protecting the poor and vulnerable.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct regular assessments of benefit levels and adjust them according to the poverty line.
gen_risks.evidence: Social protection benefits received by the bottom 40 percent of the income distribution reduced from 51 percent in 2016 to about 44 percent in 2022.

gen_risks.description: Exclusion and inclusion errors in social protection programs may lead to inadequate coverage of the poor and vulnerable.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a robust targeting system, such as the Dynamic Social Registry, to improve the accuracy of beneficiary selection.
gen_risks.evidence: Exclusion and inclusion errors remain a challenge, with nearly half (47 percent) of the poor households not covered by any social assistance program.

gen_risks.description: Climate change may exacerbate the vulnerability of the poor and vulnerable, making them more susceptible to shocks and disasters.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate change adaptation and resilience measures into social protection programs, such as the Dynamic Social Registry.
gen_risks.evidence: Bangladesh faces a high level of vulnerability to the effects of climate change, with more than 90 million Bangladeshis likely to live in ‘high climate exposure areas’.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate capacity and institutional coordination may hinder the effective implementation of social protection programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen the capacity of implementing agencies, such as the Department of Social Services, and improve institutional coordination.
gen_risks.evidence: The Department of Social Services has a strong mandate from the National Social Security Strategy, but there is scope for improved capacities and institutional coordination.

gen_risks.description: The project's reliance on a single implementing agency, the Department of Social Services, may concentrate delivery and continuity risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify implementing agencies and ensure that the Department of Social Services has a robust project implementation unit.
gen_risks.evidence: The Department of Social Services will be the nodal agency with key fiduciary responsibilities, and the project implementation unit will be set up at the Department of Social Services.

gen_risks.description: The project's financial management may be complex due to the intricacy of activity selection and various implementing agencies and finances.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire additional capacity, provide training, and conduct close monitoring to mitigate financial management-related risks.
gen_risks.evidence: The project design is complex due to the intricacy of activity selection and various implementing agencies and finances, including a mixed nature of costs, grants, cash transfers, and so on.

gen_risks.description: The project's procurement process may be affected by corruption and fraud risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct procurement in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations and ensure that the project's procurement strategy is aligned with the World Bank's Anticorruption Guidelines.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will adhere to the World Bank's Anticorruption Guidelines and ensure that procurement is conducted in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

gen_risks.description: The project's implementation may be affected by political and regulatory risks, including changes in government policies and priorities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure that the project is aligned with the government's policies and priorities, and maintain close communication with relevant government agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: The project is consistent with the World Bank Country Partnership Framework FY23–27 and the government's National Social Security Strategy.

gen_risks.description: The project's implementation may be affected by stakeholder-related risks, including inadequate engagement with beneficiaries and other stakeholders.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure that the project has a robust stakeholder engagement plan, including a communications strategy and a grievance redress mechanism.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will have a Stakeholder Engagement Plan, which will detail the grievance redress mechanism and monitoring mechanisms.

gen_risks.description: The project's implementation may be affected by environmental risks, including climate change and natural disasters.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure that the project is designed and implemented to be resilient to environmental risks, including climate change and natural disasters.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will contribute to Bangladesh's national climate adaptation strategies and will be designed and implemented to be resilient to environmental risks.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is Substantial. Safety and security concerns persist, despite the priority placed by the interim government on law and order. The interim government is implementing critical reforms before holding elections; reaching a consensus on reforms and the announcement of the election date could heighten political tensions among political parties and the interim government.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated during implementation through continuous engagement with all relevant government and nongovernmental entities, and dialogue with other stakeholders.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is Substantial. Downside risks have increased, related to uncertainties in the political process and the security situation which affects the recovery of economic activities. The financial sector remains vulnerable with deviations from international regulatory and supervisory standards and weak corporate governance. Despite recent improvements, the balance of payments remained in deficit and FX reserves remained under pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: The macroeconomic risks are partially mitigated by the GoB's reform program, supported by International Monetary Fund arrangements, as well as ongoing World Bank and other development partners' policy lending. Data show consistent budgetary and political commitment to spending on safety nets across regimes in Bangladesh, with strong stakeholder consensus on ensuring a ring-fenced core budget for social assistance and livelihoods programs for the poorest.

gt_risks.description: The Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial due to the involvement of multiple implementing agencies (the DSS and FD), the complexity of activity selection, and intervention modalities. The project's residual procurement risk specifically is also rated Substantial, due to the complexity of procurement activities, multiagency coordination, and capacity limitations (para 56, part of the Fiduciary appraisal-summary discussion immediately preceding the Key Risks section).
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigation measures include hiring additional capacity, training, and close monitoring; considering satisfactory implementation of these measures, the residual fiduciary risk is assessed as Substantial and will be managed through proactive and continuous supervision and close dialogue with the GoB. Procurement-specific mitigation: hiring full-time procurement consultants for the DSS and FD; training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, STEP, and contract management; defining clear roles and streamlining approval processes; engaging IT procurement specialists and conducting early market assessments; using performance-based KPIs in contracts and including procurement consultants on bid evaluation committees; and establishing complaint registers at both agencies, with procurement not prior-reviewed by the Bank subject to regular fiduciary reviews and post-procurement review/audit by FAPAD.

gt_risks.description: The project presents a low environmental risk and a moderate social risk, resulting in an overall moderate environmental and social (ES) risk classification. Minor environmental concerns relate to potential e-waste generation from IT equipment and increased energy use. Social risks include potential exclusion of beneficiaries, inadequate consultation, and challenges in reaching remote and marginalized communities, including those who lack IT knowledge; there is also the likelihood of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) cases given the cash transfer modalities of the project and the interaction between service providers and beneficiaries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Waste management protocols and resource efficiency measures will prevent localized pollution. The project will establish a Digital Social Registry (DSR) to improve targeting and coverage, complemented by a robust outreach and monitoring program, and will include Stakeholder Engagement Plan provisions requiring community consultation and disclosure measures. The existing DSS grievance redress mechanism (GRM) will address complaints. An SEA/SH Action Plan will be developed including code of conduct, awareness raising, and GRM to address potential incidents. The project will partially rely on the borrower's ES management framework supplemented by gap-filling measures included in the POM.
